<explanation>
Below is a step-level guide for drawing a precise system‐design/architecture diagram of the go2rtc project.  Tailor your boxes, arrows and labels to reflect the modules and interactions shown in the file tree and README.

1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose
   • It’s a monolithic, full-stack Go streaming server.  
   • Purpose: Ingest many camera/video/audio sources, perform on-the-fly transcoding via FFmpeg, and export streams via protocols (RTSP, WebRTC, HLS, MJPEG, MP4, RTMP, WebTorrent, HomeKit).

2. Top-Level Components
   • Clients   
     – Web UI (HTML/JS in www/)  
     – REST/WebSocket API clients (browsers, Home Assistant, CLI examples)  
     – RTSP clients (e.g. FFmpeg, VLC, Home Assistant)  
     – WebRTC peers (browsers, OBS via WHIP)  
     – RTMP targets (YouTube, Telegram)  
   • go2rtc Server (single Go binary)  
     A. API Module (internal/api + www static assets + openapi.yaml)  
     B. Stream Manager (internal/streams)  
     C. Source Plugins (internal/{rtsp,rtmp,http,onvif,ffmpeg,homekit,…})  
     D. Output Modules  
       – RTSP Server (internal/rtsp)  
       – RTMP Server (internal/rtmp)  
       – WebRTC Server (internal/webrtc + Pion libraries)  
       – HLS Server (internal/hls)  
       – MP4/MSE Server (internal/mp4)  
       – MJPEG Server (internal/mjpeg)  
       – WebTorrent (internal/webtorrent)  
       – HomeKit Proxy (internal/homekit)  
     E. FFmpeg Manager (internal/ffmpeg) — spawns external ffmpeg processes  
     F. ngrok Integration (internal/ngrok) for NAT traversal  
   • External Dependencies  
     – FFmpeg CLI  
     – STUN/TURN servers  
     – ngrok service  
     – Home Assistant, Docker containers, hardware devices  

3. Relationships and Data Flows
   • Clients → API Module  
     – Configuration, “Add Stream,” status, UI assets  
   • API Module ↔ Stream Manager  
     – Control plane: start/stop streams, publish endpoints  
   • Stream Manager → Source Plugins  
     – Pull or subscribe to media from cameras and devices  
   • Source Plugins → Internal Media Pipeline  
     – Normalizes incoming tracks (audio/video)  
     – Negotiates codecs, may hand off to FFmpeg Manager for transcoding  
   • Media Pipeline → Output Modules  
     – Streams data to clients via RTSP/RTMP/WebRTC/HLS/MP4/MJPEG/WebTorrent/HomeKit  
   • Output Modules → Clients/External Services  
     – RTSP: clients at rtsp://…  
     – WebRTC: peer connections (UDP/TCP)  
     – HLS/MP4/MJPEG: HTTP endpoints  
     – RTMP: push to external RTMP URLs  
     – ngrok & STUN/TURN assist WebRTC NAT traversal  

4. Architectural Patterns and Principles
   • Layered modular monolith – clear separation of control plane (API) and data plane (streams)  
   • Plugin-style source/output modules under internal/ and pkg/  
   • Event-driven lifecycle – streams started on-demand, stopped when idle  
   • Zero-config “auto” streams via Home Assistant import or empty config  

5. Technologies and Frameworks
   • Go modules for: HTTP API (internal/api), WebSocket, RTSP, WebRTC (Pion), HLS, MJPEG, MP4, ngrok  
   • FFmpeg CLI spawned on demand for transcoding via internal/ffmpeg  
   • Static web UI in www/ served by API module  
   • OpenAPI spec in api/openapi.yaml for client integration  
   • Docker build definitions in docker/  
   • Examples in examples/ demonstrating client usage  

6. Tailoring the Diagram
   • Emphasize the clear separation:
     – Control Plane: API, static UI, scripting (scripts/)  
     – Data Plane: Stream Manager, Source Plugins, Output Modules  
   • For a streaming server, show both directions:
     – Ingress: Sensors/Cameras → Source Plugins  
     – Egress: Server → Clients & Services  

7. Diagramming Guidelines
   • Use boxes for each major component (API, Stream Manager, each Source Plugin group, each Output Module).  
   • Draw directional arrows to show data/control flow.  
   • Color code:
     – Blue: External systems (clients, cameras, services)  
     – Green: Core go2rtc modules  
     – Orange: External dependencies (FFmpeg, ngrok, STUN/TURN)  
   • Label each arrow with protocol names (e.g. RTSP pull, HTTP API, WebSocket, RTP, RTMP push).  
   • Denote optional/conditional flows (e.g. dashed arrows for optional ngrok or TURN).  
   • Include notes on ports (1984 HTTP, 8554 RTSP, 8555 WebRTC) and basic auth points.

Putting it all together, your diagram might look like:

 [Clients: Browser / HA / FFmpeg / OBS]  
       ↕ REST / WS            ↕ RTSP                 ↕ WebRTC  
   [API Module] ←─────────→ [Stream Manager] ←─── Source Plugins (RTSP, HTTP, ONVIF, HomeKit,…)  
                               │  
                             FFmpeg Manager  
                               │  
   ┌───────────┬───────────┬───────┬───────┐  
   │ RTSP SRV  │ RTMP SRV  │ WebRTC│ HLS   │ …  
   └───────────┴───────────┴───────┴───────┘  
       ↓            ↓            ↓         ↓  
   [Clients & External Services: VLC, YT, Tg, Browsers]  

Use this template as the basis; expand each box to show sub‐packages (internal/streams, internal/ffmpeg, etc.) as needed for internal documentation.
</explanation>
